turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.


New instance. Task id: task-8933d938

description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances with cost-aware demonstrations and the required per-turn action protocol.

# Continual-ARC

1. Treat each instance independently. Read its test grid, task id, action choices, and remaining demo/attempt caps. Advance the puzzle by putting exactly one valid action JSON object on the final line; unrelated tool calls do not submit or request a demo.
2. Infer the transformation from demonstrations and the test grid. Separate observed facts from hypotheses, and check that the examples actually cover the test's structure. When they do not, do not turn a plausible pattern into a confident rule.
3. Request one more demo when its likely information can distinguish live hypotheses and is worth its one-point cost. Incorporate that pair before deciding again; don't request repeatedly without reassessing whether another example can change the answer. Compare this cost with the one-point cost of a wrong submission and the remaining caps.
4. Submit a complete grid when the rule is sufficiently supported; verify dimensions (1–30) and cell values (0–9). Use `finish` only after the instance is over, and stop when the instance has ended.
